extracted.intended_audience: institutional investment managers, covered persons to securities loans, registered national securities associations (RNSAs), securities market participants, and securities/regulatory counsel
extracted.subtask_description: An SEC Federal Register notice/order granting temporary exemptions from compliance with Rule 13f-2 (Form SHO) and certain aspects of Rule 10c-1a, explaining statutory authority, the Commission's findings, the Court remand, and specifying exemption durations and effective dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 13f-2 filing requirement (Form SHO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 13f-2 requires institutional investment managers that meet or exceed certain specified thresholds to file Form SHO, in accordance with the form's instructions, with the Commission within 14 calendar days after the end of each calendar month with regard to certain equity securities via the Commission's EDGAR system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing must be via EDGAR and in accordance with the form's instructions; the rule applies to managers meeting the rule's specified thresholds. (See text: 'file Form SHO ... with the Commission within 14 calendar days after the end of each calendar month ... via the Commission's Electronic Data Gathering, Analysis, and Retrieval (“EDGAR”) system.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission publication of aggregated Form SHO data
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will publish, on an aggregated basis, certain information regarding each equity security reported by institutional investment managers on Form SHO and filed with the Commission via the EDGAR system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported Form SHO data will be aggregated and published by the Commission; this is a transparency/data-publication obligation tied to Rule 13f-2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 10c-1a reporting obligation for covered persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 10c-1a requires that any covered person who agrees to a covered securities loan on behalf of itself or another person must report, within certain time periods, certain information to a registered national securities association (RNSA) or rely on a reporting agent to fulfill its reporting obligations under certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule specifies time periods and what information must be reported (the notice references 'within certain time periods, certain information'); entities may rely on reporting agents where permitted by the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: RNSA duties under Rule 10c-1a (format, public data, retention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 10c-1a requires that an RNSA implement rules regarding the format and manner of its collection of Rule 10c-1a information, make publicly available certain data pertaining to reported securities, and comply with certain data retention and availability requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RNSAs must adopt collection/format rules, provide public access to specified data, and meet retention/availability obligations (see citations to 17 CFR 240.10c-1a(f), (g), (h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for exemptions under Section 13(f)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 13(f)(3) of the Exchange Act authorizes the Commission, by rule or order, to exempt, conditionally or unconditionally, any institutional investment manager or security, or any class of institutional investment managers or securities from any or all of the provisions of Section 13(f) of the Exchange Act or the rules thereunder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions under 13(f)(3) may be granted by rule or order and may be conditional or unconditional; used here as the authority for temporary exemptive relief from Rule 13f-2/Form SHO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for exemptions under Section 36(a)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 36(a)(1) of the Exchange Act authorizes the Commission, by rule, regulation, or order, to exempt, conditionally or unconditionally, any person, security, or transaction, or any class or classes of persons, securities, or transactions, from any provision or provisions of the Exchange Act, or of any rule or regulation thereunder, to the extent that such exemption is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, and is consistent with the protection of investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard for granting exemptions under 36(a)(1) is that the exemption be necessary or appropriate in the public interest and consistent with investor protection; this is the legal test the Commission applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court remand and requirement to consider economic impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit remanded, without vacatur, the Rules to the Commission to allow the agency to consider and quantify the cumulative economic impact of the Rules, consistent with the Court's opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission must consider and quantify cumulative economic impacts in responding to the remand; the remand prompted the Commission's decision to provide temporary exemptions while undertaking further analysis or potential amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission's public-interest/investor-protection finding for temporary exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission finds these temporary exemptions to be necessary in the public interest and consistent with the protection of investors because they will allow the Commission time to respond to the Court's opinion and take any further appropriate actions, which may include proposing amendments to the Rules, and allow these actions to occur in a manner that could minimize potential costs entities may incur to comply with any provisions of the Rules that could change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification ties the exemption to procedural needs (time to respond/consider amendments) and to minimizing potential compliance costs while maintaining investor protection; this is the policy rationale the Commission uses when exercising exemption authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific temporary exemption orders and effective/end dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission grants temporary exemptive relief from compliance with Rule 13f-2 and Form SHO reporting effective January 2, 2026, and ending January 2, 2028; and grants temporary exemptive relief from compliance with Rule 10c-1a regarding the reporting date until September 28, 2028, and from compliance with Rules 10c-1a(g) and (h)(3) regarding the dissemination date until March 29, 2029.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational effect: entities need not comply with the specified obligations during these exemption periods; the notice also clarifies that Form SHO reports for the January 2028 reporting period would be required to be filed within 14 calendar days after the end of January 2028 (i.e., compliance resumes at the end of the exemption period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file Form SHO 'in accordance with the form's instructions' via EDGAR
rubrics_metrics.description: Form SHO filings must be made 'in accordance with the form's instructions' and submitted via the Commission's EDGAR system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adherence to form instructions is an express requirement of Rule 13f-2; technical/formal compliance (data format, fields, and EDGAR submission) is required when the rule is in effect.
